summary: Returns the value as `NaN`, or throws.
description: Nothing is coerced first, which is where this differs from the global `isNaN`: that one converts its argument, so `isNaN("abc")` and `isNaN(undefined)` both report `true`.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not the `NaN` number.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNaN(NaN); // => NaN
requireNaN(0 / 0); // => 0 / 0
requireNaN(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNaN("abc"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
